bugs_found: `all` returns 0 when `.banking-profile` is absent, so deleting the profile disables the banking gate.
Malformed or non-mapping profiles are trusted by subcommands; valid YAML like a list/scalar can crash on `.get()` or bypass schema assumptions.
Sensitive paths that match no files, unreadable files, or undecodable files can be silently skipped in `contract-validate`/`floats-check`, allowing CI to pass without checking target code.
`contract-presence` only compares contract `name` values to function names globally per file; misplaced contracts, duplicate method names, or fake blocks can satisfy unrelated functions.
Non-Python sensitive files are only warned in `contract-presence`, so banking logic in TS/Go/Java can pass without contracts.
`floats-check` misses real precision hazards such as float literals, arithmetic, `Decimal(float)`, and JavaScript numeric money operations.
`review-gate` does not enforce the documented latest-overall verdict=approve condition; a later non-code-reviewer request-changes round can be ignored.
Finding dedup overwrites the entire finding by id, so a later duplicate can downgrade blocker/major severity instead of resolving it and bypass the gate.
`review-gate` trusts unvalidated JSON and filename order; malformed/directly invoked review artifacts can crash or produce stale ack resolution decisions.
